# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS | **Section:** Aseneth's Beauty and Status

---

**1:1** In the first year of the seven years of plenty, in the second month, on the fifth day of the month, Pharaoh sent Joseph to travel throughout all the land of Egypt.

**1:2** Joseph came into the district of Heliopolis and gathered the grain of that region, which was like the sand of the sea.

**1:3** There was a man in that city, a priest of Heliopolis named Pentephres. He was a satrap of Pharaoh and his chief official — a great and powerful man throughout all Egypt.

**1:4** Pentephres had a virgin daughter, eighteen years old, tall, beautiful, and graceful, surpassing all the virgins of the earth. She bore no resemblance to the Egyptian women but was in every respect like the daughters of the Hebrews.

**1:5** She was tall like Sarah, beautiful like Rebekah, and graceful like Rachel.

**1:6** The virgin's name was Aseneth.

**1:7** The fame of her beauty spread throughout the land and to the ends of the inhabited world. All the sons of rulers, satraps, and kings — young men of power — sought her as a wife.

**1:8** There was great rivalry among them on account of Aseneth, and they were ready to fight one another because of her.

**1:9** Even Pharaoh's firstborn son heard of her and begged his father to give her to him as a wife.

**1:10** He said to him: "Give me Aseneth, the daughter of Pentephres the priest of Heliopolis, as my wife."

**1:11** But his father Pharaoh said to him: "Why do you seek a wife beneath your rank? You are king and ruler over all Egypt. The daughter of the king of Moab is betrothed to you, and she is a queen. Take her as your wife."

**1:12** Aseneth despised all men and held them in contempt. No man had ever seen her, because Pentephres had built adjoining his house a great and very high tower.

**1:13** The upper story of that tower had ten rooms. The first was large and beautiful, paved with purple stone, its walls lined with precious and multicolored stones, and its ceiling of gold.

**1:14** Fixed within it were countless idols of Egypt made of gold and silver, and Aseneth worshiped them all, feared them, and sacrificed to them every day.

**1:15** The second room held all of Aseneth's adornments and her seven virgin attendants, born the same night as she, whom she loved greatly.

**1:16** The third room held all Aseneth's treasures — much gold and silver, gold-woven garments, precious and costly stones, and fine linen.

**1:17** The remaining seven rooms belonged to the seven virgins, one room each.

**1:18** A stone staircase of thirty-two steps led from the ground to the uppermost story.

**1:19** The windows of the upper room faced east and south; there were also windows facing north to admit the cooling breeze.

---
